statements.AUTHOR-007: When an approved requirement is minted, the req-author skill shall write it through the real spec req CLI, never by editing SPEC.json directly.
statements.CHCK-007: If a code tag references a deprecated requirement, then spec check shall report DEPRECATED_REFERENCED as an error.
statements.CHCK-008: If a domain declares the ears grammar and an Active or Draft statement does not match one of the five EARS shapes, then spec check shall report STATEMENT_GRAMMAR at the domain's declared severity, defaulting to warning.
statements.CHCK-012: The spec check command shall report integrity diagnostics across every member repo, each row carrying a code, a severity, and the offending location.
statements.CHCK-014: When spec check runs with --ci, the command shall delete the existing index and rebuild it cold before evaluating diagnostics.
statements.CHCK-016: If a requirement's cites entry resolves to no term, then spec check shall report UNDEFINED_TERM as an error.
statements.CHCK-017: If an Active term is cited by no requirement, then spec check shall report ORPHAN_TERM as a warning.
statements.CHCK-018: If a requirement's citation pins an older version than the cited term's current version, then spec check shall report TERM_DRIFT as a warning until spec term confirm re-pins it.
statements.CHCK-019: If a requirement cites a superseded term id, then spec check shall report SUPERSEDED_TERM_REFERENCED as an error until spec term confirm re-points the citation to the successor.
statements.CHCK-020: When spec glossary runs, the command shall regenerate GLOSSARY.md from the term store deterministically, byte-identical across runs over the same store.
statements.CHCK-021: When spec glossary --migrate runs, the command shall parse each committed GLOSSARY.md bullet into a term entry in document order, skipping when the term store already holds entries.
statements.CHCK-022: When spec glossary --check runs and the committed GLOSSARY.md differs byte-for-byte from the generated output, the command shall exit 1.
statements.CHCK-023: While the platform is a git repository with a resolvable HEAD, spec check shall report REQUIREMENT_REMOVED for any requirement present at HEAD that is absent from the working tree without a supersession in the same change, with no flag required.
statements.CHCK-024: If the committed GLOSSARY.md does not byte-match the glossary generated from the TERM store, then spec check shall report GLOSSARY_DRIFT as a warning.
statements.CHCK-025: When spec check finds a sibling directory without a spec-engine.member.json, the command shall report NO_SPEC_CONFIG at warning severity.
statements.CHCK-029: If a requirement's supersedes pointer names an id that does not exist or names the requirement itself, then spec check shall report BROKEN_SUPERSEDE at error severity.
statements.CHCK-034: If an implementing or documenting @spec tag references a Draft requirement, then spec check shall report DRAFT_REFERENCED at warning severity.
statements.CHCK-035: The spec check command shall report UNVERIFIED_REQ at warning severity by default.
statements.CHCK-036: When spec-engine/check.json declares a severity rule for a diagnostic code, spec check shall grade every row of that code to the rule's severity of error, warning, or off.
statements.CHCK-037: When a severity rule carries a match list of domain keys or requirement ids, spec check shall apply it only to rows whose requirement is listed or carries a listed key, the most specific rule winning.
statements.CHCK-038: When a diagnostic row is graded off, spec check shall omit it from every output.
statements.CHCK-039: If spec-engine/check.json fails its schema, then spec check shall exit 2 naming the file and the failing path.
statements.CHCK-040: If a domain declares the ears grammar and the text after the first shall in an Active or Draft statement contains a semicolon followed by whitespace, then spec check shall report STATEMENT_GRAMMAR at the domain's declared severity.
statements.CHCK-041: If a domain declares the ears grammar and an Active or Draft statement's result continues with a comma-and clause that names its own subject before another shall, then spec check shall report STATEMENT_GRAMMAR at the domain's declared severity.
statements.CHCK-042: If a domain declares the ears grammar and an Active or Draft statement carries a rationale connective, then spec check shall report STATEMENT_GRAMMAR at the domain's declared severity.
statements.CHCK-043: When spec check finds at least one error-severity diagnostic, the command shall exit 1.
statements.CHCK-044: When spec check finds only warning-severity diagnostics, the command shall exit 0.
statements.CHCK-049: When an Active statement breaks a rule, spec check shall report STATEMENT_RULES at the rule's configured severity, error by default, one row per rule per statement.
statements.CHCK-050: spec lint shall print every finding for the platform, one domain, or one requirement, and exit 1 when there is any.
statements.CHCK-051: spec lint shall check Active requirements by default and Draft requirements too under --all.
statements.CHRT-010: When a domain envelope carrying a scope field is written and re-read, the spec engine shall preserve the scope field unchanged.
statements.CHRT-011: When spec domain list --json runs, the command shall emit a key-sorted array of {key, scope} objects, with null for a domain without a scope and [] for a platform with no domains.
statements.CHRT-012: When spec req <domain> resolves its target domain, the command shall print that domain's charter to stderr while leaving the piped next-id and --json stdout byte-identical.
statements.CHRT-014: The statement rules shall report a statement that is more than one sentence, or that has no closing period.
statements.CHRT-015: The statement rules shall report a statement longer than the configured maximum, 280 characters by default.
statements.CHRT-016: The statement rules shall report a statement that names a file or folder of the repository.
statements.CHRT-017: The statement rules shall report a statement that describes how a test is written.
statements.CHRT-018: The statement rules shall report a statement that describes CI or tooling layout.
statements.CHRT-019: The statement rules shall report a statement that tells how the requirement changed over time.
statements.CHRT-020: The statement rules shall report a statement that uses a word from the configured jargon list.
statements.CHRT-021: The statement rules shall report a statement that names which tool is in use.
statements.CHRT-022: The statement rules shall skip glossary terms.
statements.DIST-005: The spec docs command shall serve the prebuilt documentation site over HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1 only, with no flag to widen the bind address.
statements.DIST-006: When run with --probe, spec docs shall boot on an ephemeral loopback port, fetch /, and exit 0 only when the site title renders (exit 1 otherwise).
statements.DIST-008: If no docs root exists, then spec docs shall exit 2 with guidance naming bun run build:site.
statements.DOMAIN-012: When normalization changed the input name, spec domain new shall print exactly one <raw> → <KEY> transformation line, and shall print no such line when the input was already canonical.
statements.DOMAIN-013: If the normalized domain key does not match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$/, then spec domain new shall print an error to stderr and exit 2.
statements.DOMAIN-018: If spec domain list runs where spec-engine/ is missing or not a directory, then it shall print the friendly not-a-platform message and exit 2.
statements.INDX-011: The scanner shall derive a tag's kind from its file path — a tag in a test file verifies, a tag in any other file implements — and the tag itself never states the kind.
statements.INDX-015: When a tag's file ends in _test.go, _test.rs, _spec.lua, or _test.lua, or lives under a spec/ directory, the scanner shall classify the tag as verifies, alongside the .test., .spec., tests/, __tests__/, and e2e paths it already recognizes.
statements.INIT-032: When a declared member is present on disk without a spec-engine.member.json, the index shall emit one warning-severity NO_SPEC_CONFIG diagnostic naming the member and suggesting spec init <name>.
statements.PROOF-015: While test results are supplied, spec check shall mark an active requirement PROVEN only when at least one verifying tag correlates to a passing test.
statements.PROOF-016: While test results are supplied, spec check shall report UNPROVEN_REQ for an active requirement whose verifying tags all fail or lack a correlated test.
statements.PROV-005: The spec CLI shall store and display an issue id verbatim as an opaque string.
statements.PROV-006: The spec engine shall never resolve an issue id against the requirements table or use it as a key that routes or merges provenance between requirements.
statements.QURY-004: When searching requirements, spec query shall exclude deprecated requirements from the results.
statements.QURY-006: When searching requirements, spec query shall exclude superseded requirements from the results.
statements.REQ-027: If spec req is run against a directory containing no spec-engine/ directory, then it shall print the friendly not-a-platform guidance and exit 2.
statements.REQ-038: When a lifecycle command is invoked through any surface, the spec engine shall run every guard before the first byte is written.
statements.SCHM-010: Where a domain envelope declares grammar and grammarSeverity, the shared schema shall validate and preserve both fields through every read and write.
statements.SCHM-012: The CLI/webapp/MCP read surfaces shall return identical data for the same query over the same platform state.
statements.SCHM-015: If any envelope touched by a write operation fails schema validation, then the spec CLI shall persist no changes to any SPEC.json file.
statements.SCHM-016: When a domain envelope carrying term, aliases, cites, or section fields is written and re-read, the spec engine shall preserve those fields unchanged.
statements.SCHM-024: When a requirement is authored or amended through the CLI, the HTTP API, or the MCP server, the spec engine shall write the same envelope for the same inputs.
statements.SCHM-031: When the validating write seam rewrites an existing SPEC.json, it shall leave every unchanged entry byte-identical.
statements.SCHM-032: When the validating write seam changes an existing entry, it shall patch the entry in its existing key order and add a defaulted field only where the file already carries that key.
statements.SCHM-033: When the validating write seam appends an entry to an existing SPEC.json, it shall give the entry the key order of the last existing entry.
statements.SERV-006: Where a feature's flag is not enabled, the webapp shall refuse every surface of that feature — the page serves a coming-soon document and its endpoints respond 404.
statements.SERV-007: When the SPEC_FLAGS environment variable lists a feature key, spec serve shall enable that feature's nav link, page, and endpoints together.
statements.SERV-009: The spec serve /api/* read routes — coverage / report / requirements / query / resolve / relations / propagation — shall each return the same deterministic JSON shape as the corresponding CLI --json command.
statements.SERV-014: When rendering the Coverage and Requirements pages without ?all=1, the webapp shall list only requirements that are neither Superseded nor Deprecated, omitting any domain left with no listed requirement.
statements.SERV-015: When the query string carries all=1, the Coverage and Requirements pages shall list the full ledger, Superseded and Deprecated requirements included.
statements.SERV-028: When the spec mcp server receives a spec_req tool call, the spec mcp command shall author the requirement through the mint operation and return the spec req --json shape.
statements.SERV-029: When the spec mcp server receives a spec_amend tool call, the spec mcp command shall revise the requirement through the amend operation and return the spec amend --json shape.
statements.SERV-030: When the spec mcp server receives a spec_move tool call, the spec mcp command shall move the requirement through the move operation and return the spec move --json shape.
statements.SERV-031: When spec serve receives POST /api/requirements/:id/move with the editor feature enabled, the spec serve command shall move the requirement through the move operation under the write lock and return the spec move --json shape.
